records.question: How long does Spotify hold on to my personal information?
records.text:
Spotify keeps personal data only as long as is necessary to provide the Spotify Service and for Spotify's legitimate and essential business purposes, such as maintaining the service's performance, making data-driven business decisions, complying with legal obligations, and resolving disputes [Spotify – 6. Data retention].

Specific retention periods include:
*   **Data that expires after a specific period of time:** Personal data entered in search queries is deleted after 90 days [Spotify – 6. Data retention].
*   **Data retained until your Spotify account is deleted:** Spotify keeps data like your Spotify username and profile information, as well as streaming history, for as long as the account exists, which is used for personalized recommendations and retrospective playlists [Spotify – 6. Data retention]. When the account is deleted, this data is either deleted or de-identified [Spotify – 6. Data retention].
*   **Data retained until you remove it:** You have the right to request the deletion of certain personal data, and you can also delete some data directly within the Spotify Service, such as your profile picture [Spotify – 6. Data retention].
*   **Data retained for extended time periods for limited purposes:** After an account is deleted, some data may be kept longer for limited reasons, such as fulfilling legal or contractual obligations, government orders for investigations, or for litigation. This data may also be kept for a limited time to ensure user safety or protect against harmful content [Spotify – 6. Data retention].
*   **Age Check Data:** This data is deleted immediately after the Age Check is completed [Spotify – 6. Data retention].

records.question: Can other people read my Zoom Email messages?
records.text: Account owners and designated account administrators can access email and calendar content sent to and from users on their Zoom Email or Zoom Calendar accounts, even if those Zoom Emails are encrypted, depending on their settings [Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?]. Recipients of Zoom Emails can see, save, and share your email content with others, including by sharing emails to Zoom Team Chat [Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?]. If encrypted content is shared, such as an encrypted Zoom Email to Zoom Team Chat or forwarded to a third-party recipient without a Zoom Email account, Zoom will not end-to-end encrypt the shared or forwarded content [Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?].
cited_labels: [Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?]

records.question: Do I give up my right to a jury if I have a dispute with Coursera?
records.text: Yes, you are waiving your right to have a jury trial when pursuing disputes or claims against Coursera [Coursera – Thank you for using Coursera!]. Furthermore, you and Coursera are electing that all Claims be resolved by arbitration, meaning there is no judge or jury in arbitration [Coursera – 15. Binding Arbitration and Class Action Waiver]. You are also waiving your constitutional and statutory rights to sue in court and have a trial in front of a judge or a jury [Coursera – 15. Binding Arbitration and Class Action Waiver].
cited_labels: [Coursera – 15. Binding Arbitration and Class Action Waiver]

records.question: How long does Coursera store my personal information?
records.text: Coursera keeps your Personal Data for no longer than necessary for the purposes it was collected and processed, to comply with legal and regulatory obligations, to exercise legal rights, and to protect against legal claims [Coursera – Retention of Personal Data]. The retention time depends on the purpose of collection, the nature of your interaction with them, or as required by applicable laws to establish, exercise, or defend legal rights [Coursera – Retention of Personal Data].

records.question: Could Coursera still have my data after I ask them to erase it?
records.text: Yes, after you request deletion, Coursera may retain limited Personal Data for lawful and legitimate purposes, which can differ based on your location, such as fulfilling legal obligations [Coursera – Your Rights]. Additionally, residual information might remain in their databases, access logs, or other records, and this information may or may not include your Personal Data [Coursera – Your Rights].

records.question: Can a teenager sign up for their own PayPal account?
records.text: To open an account, you must either be an individual who is at least 18 years old or a business that can form a legally binding contract [Paypal – Opening an account].

records.question: How long does PayPal keep my information once I stop being a customer?
records.text:
For the duration of the relationship, Personal Information is stored for the relationship's duration plus 10 years, or as required by local law after the relationship ends, unless keeping it longer is permitted by applicable law [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information].

If you close your account or profile, PayPal may still keep some Personal Information so it can:
* Complete a transaction, provide requested goods or services, or comply with promises in the user agreement or contract [Paypal – Your rights].
* Detect and prevent fraudulent, malicious, or illegal activity [Paypal – Your rights].
* Protect legal rights [Paypal – Your rights].
* Manage internal business processes related to your expectations when using the Services [Paypal – Your rights].
* Comply with laws and other legal or governmental requirements [Paypal – Your rights].

Additionally, PayPal may retain electronic money after an account closure for the time reasonably needed to protect itself and/or any third party against risks like reversals, fees, fines, penalties, and other liabilities [Paypal – Closing Your PayPal Account].

Biometric data is retained for as long as needed or permitted for its purpose, and no more than 3 years after your account closes, unless applicable law requires otherwise [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information].

Personal Information is also retained for the minimum necessary time when retention is advisable for litigation, investigations, audit, and compliance practices, or to protect against legal claims [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information].
cited_labels: [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information]

records.question: If I close my Strava account, does my data actually go away?
records.text: After you request account deletion, your personal information is permanently and irreversibly deleted from Strava's systems, including backups [Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data]. However, it may take up to 45 days for your personal information and system logs to be fully deleted from their systems following account deletion [Strava – Retention of Information] [Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data]. Additionally, Strava may retain information even after deletion requests to comply with the law or take other actions permitted by law [Strava – Retention of Information] [Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data]. Content or information might remain available even after you delete your account or specific information from your profile [Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data].

records.question: Does Pinterest use the websites I visit to show me ads?
records.text: Yes, Pinterest may show you ads both on and off Pinterest [Pinterest – We also use your information to personalize the ads you see]. For instance, if you show interest in camping tents on Pinterest or look at sleeping bags on a partner's website, Pinterest might show you ads for other outdoor products [Pinterest – We also use your information to personalize the ads you see]. Pinterest also advertises Pinterest products and services on other sites by disclosing information like cookie IDs, your IP address, and a hashed version of your email address to marketing services [Pinterest – To deliver ads, off Pinterest, that are relevant, interesting and personal to you about Pinterest, we:] [Pinterest – We also use your information to personalize the ads you see].
